### Observed differences

- Six activities — A28, A30, A31, A32, A33 and A34 — appeared in roughly half of the traces in the earlier window (49–52 in 100) and in almost every trace in the later window (99–100 in 100), each occurring at most once per trace in both windows. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- In the earlier window, the two sets {A28, A30, A31} and {A32, A33, A34} were alternatives: cross-set pairs never occurred in the same trace (0 in 100), and each set appeared alone in about half of the traces. In the later window, cross-set pairs occur together in about 98 in 100 traces, always with a first-set activity before a second-set activity. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024]
- A25, present in all traces, preceded whichever set ran in the earlier window (co-occurrence with each of the six at 49–52 in 100, A25 alone otherwise); in the later window it precedes each of the six in about 99 in 100 traces. A26 similarly moved from following only one set per trace to following each of the six in about 99 in 100 traces. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- Successor profiles agree: A25 now leads almost only to A28/A30/A31 (its share of outgoing transitions to A32 fell from about 16 in 100 to under 1 in 100, with A33/A34 no longer observed), and A28/A30/A31 now lead into the second set instead of directly to A26 (A26's share of A28's outgoing transitions fell from about 36 in 100 to under 1 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Within each set the order remains unfixed (e.g., A28 before A30 in about 49 in 100 co-occurrences in the later window, A30 before A28 in about 50 in 100), so no new fixed order emerged inside the sets. [REL013, REL014, REL018, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- Positions and gaps are consistent with an inserted block: A25's mean relative position moved earlier (0.67 to 0.62) and A26's later (0.80 to 0.83); the step distance from A25 to the second-set activities and from first-set activities to A26 grew from 1–3 steps to 4–5 steps. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]
- On the timing side, the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A20 and A27 roughly doubled (median about 0.93 h to 1.84 h), as did the elapsed time between completions of A29 and A27 (median about 0.14 h to 0.33 h). [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in the middle of the process: the two three-activity sets {A28, A30, A31} and {A32, A33, A34}, which in the earlier window were mutually exclusive alternatives (one set per trace, in roughly equal shares, never both), were in the later window executed together in essentially every trace in a fixed sequence A25 → {A28/A30/A31, any internal order} → {A32/A33/A34, any internal order} → A26, turning all six activities from optional (about 50 in 100 traces) into effectively mandatory (99–100 in 100). The relational evidence shows this directly — cross-set co-occurrence rose from 0 to about 98 in 100 with a fixed inter-set order — and participation, successor, position and gap indicators all agree; the volume of qualifying control-flow items (51 against about 0.6 expected without a change) rules out a chance explanation for the family as a whole. Limitations: about 2 in 100 later traces still show only one of the sets, so the old either/or behaviour may persist rarely, and a change in the mix of cases entering the process, rather than in the process itself, cannot be ruled out from these two windows alone. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL015, REL019, REL022, DIR001, DIR002, POS003, POS006, LAG001, LAG004]

Other differences: a timing change stands apart from this hypothesis — the elapsed time between consecutive completion events roughly doubled on two transitions (A20→A27: median about 0.93 h to 1.84 h; A29→A27: about 0.14 h to 0.33 h), a timing hypothesis in its own right whose connection to the structural change the evidence cannot establish. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 145 units tested, 0.6 items expected without change overall. By family:
- control_flow: 118 units tested, 51 items, 0.59 expected without change. 51 items vs 0.59 expected — that's ~86 times the chance expectation. Massively more than chance.
- time: 27 units tested, 2 items, 0.013 expected. 2 items vs 0.013 expected — about 150 times the expectation. Also far more than chance.

So the screening comparison says: the number of items is many times larger than expected by chance in both families. So we move on to judging by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

Now let's understand the behavioural picture.

Activities involved: A25, A26, A28, A30, A31, A32, A33, A34, plus time items involving A20, A27, A29.

OCC items:
- A28, A30, A31: participation 0.485 → 0.985 (about 49 in 100 traces → about 99 in 100). Mean occurrences per trace same (recurrence 0, so once per trace max).
- A32, A33, A34: participation 0.515 → 0.995 (about 52 in 100 → about 100 in 100).

So six activities (A28, A30, A31, A32, A33, A34) went from occurring in roughly half of traces to nearly all traces. They became mandatory (or near-mandatory) instead of optional.

REL items:
- REL001-003 (A25 with A28/A30/A31): before, co-occurrence 0.485, A25-only 0.515; after, co-occurrence 0.985, A25-only 0.015. Order: A25 before B always (A_before_B 0.485 → 0.985). So before, in about half the traces A25 occurred without A28/A30/A31; after, they almost always occur together, with A25 first.
- REL004-006 (A25 with A32/A33/A34): same pattern, co-occurrence 0.515 → 0.995.
- REL007-012 (A26 with A28/A30/A31 and A32/A33/A34): before, co-occurrence ~0.485-0.515, A26-only ~0.5; after co-occurrence ~0.985-0.995, B_before_A (i.e., A28 before A26 etc.) ~0.985. So A26 now almost always co-occurs with each of the six, and the six activities come before A26.
- REL013, 014, 018 (A28-A30, A28-A31, A30-A31): before, co-occurrence 0.485, neither 0.515, and when they co-occur, order is mixed (A_before_B ~0.24, B_before_A ~0.245). After: co-occurrence 0.985, neither 0.015, order still mixed (A_before_B ~0.44-0.55, B_before_A ~0.435-0.545). So these three activities among themselves have no fixed order — they co-occur in both orders. That's consistent with them being parallel/concurrent.
- REL015-017, 019-024 (pairs between {A28,A30,A31} and {A32,A33,A34}): before, co-occurrence 0.0 — A_only 0.485, B_only 0.515. So before, these two groups were alternatives: exactly one of the two groups occurred per trace. After: co-occurrence 0.98, A_before_B 0.98. So after, both groups occur in every trace, first group {A28,A30,A31} before second group {A32,A33,A34}.
- REL025-027 (A32-A33, A32-A34, A33-A34): before, co-occurrence 0.515, neither 0.485, mixed order; after co-occurrence 0.995, mixed order. So {A32,A33,A34} are concurrent among themselves.

So the picture: Before, the process had a choice: either the group {A28, A30, A31} (in ~49% of traces) or the group {A32, A33, A34} (in ~52% of traces), never both. A25 occurred in all traces and preceded whichever group occurred; A26 occurred in all traces and followed whichever group occurred. After: both groups occur in every trace, {A28,A30,A31} first (before A26, after A25), then {A32,A33,A34}, then A26. Wait — let me check ordering with A25 and A26.

REL001: A25 before A28 (A_before_B where A=A25, B=A28) 0.985 after. REL007: A26 with A28: B_before_A = A28 before A26, 0.985 after. So order: A25 → {A28,A30,A31} (mutually unordered) → {A32,A33,A34} (mutually unordered) → A26.

Before: A25 → one of the two groups → A26. The groups were alternatives (XOR choice).

After: A25 → {A28,A30,A31} → {A32,A33,A34} → A26. Both groups always executed.

So the change: a previously exclusive choice between two blocks became a sequence of both blocks. This is a structural change: the second block was added after the first (or the choice was removed). Activities became mandatory rather than optional/alternative.

DIR items:
- DIR001 (A25): before, outgoing transitions distributed to A34 (0.19), A28 (0.17), A32 (0.155), A33 (0.17), A30 (0.17), A31 (0.145) — i.e., A25 led to whichever group member was chosen (roughly uniform over the six). After: A30 0.375, A28 0.31, A31 0.30 — A25 now leads only to the first group {A28,A30,A31} (roughly uniform among the three), and no longer to A32/A33/A34 directly (A32 0.005, A33/A34 absent). Consistent.
- DIR002 (A28): before, A28 led to A31, A26, A30 (the other members of its group and A26). After: A28 leads to A30, A31, A32, A34, A33 — i.e., to its group peers and to the second group. A26 dropped from 0.36 to 0.005. Consistent with insertion of the second block between the first block and A26.
- DIR003 (A30): before A26 0.34, A28 0.30, A31 0.36; after A31 0.43, A28 0.26, A32 0.12, A34 0.10, A33 0.10; A26 gone. Consistent.
- DIR004 (A31): similar.

POS items:
- A25 position mean 0.671 → 0.620 (moved slightly earlier in relative position; consistent with more activities after it).
- A26 position mean 0.801 → 0.827 (moved later; consistent with more activities before it).
- A28/A30/A31: support 0.485 → 0.985, position mean ~0.74 → ~0.68 (earlier, because the second block now follows).
- A32/A33/A34: support 0.515 → 0.995, position mean ~0.73 → ~0.77 (later, because they now come after the first block).

LAG items:
- LAG001-003 (A25 → A32/A33/A34): before, gaps 1-3 steps; after, gaps 4-5 steps. Because the first block now sits between A25 and the second block.
- LAG004-006 (A28/A30/A31 → A26): before gaps 1-3; after gaps 4-5. Because the second block now sits between.

All consistent with: previously A25 → (choice of one block) → A26; now A25 → block1 → block2 → A26.

Time items:
- TWAIT001 (A20 → A27): elapsed time between consecutive completions went from median ~0.93 h to ~1.84 h (mean 0.93 → 1.85, roughly doubled). Counts 94 → 105.
- TWAIT002 (A29 → A27): median ~0.14 h → ~0.33 h (mean 0.19 → 0.40, roughly doubled). Counts 106 → 95.

Both time items show roughly a doubling of elapsed time between consecutive completion events. Time family: 2 items vs 0.013 expected — far above chance. These support a timing hypothesis: inter-event times roughly doubled at two transitions. Note TWAIT is elapsed time between consecutive completion events — not pure waiting/service time.

Now the hypothesis judgement:

Control flow: 51 items vs 0.59 expected — many times larger. The evidence is direct and consistent: OCC (participation), REL (co-occurrence and order), DIR (successor redistribution), POS, LAG all tell one coherent story: two alternative blocks became a fixed sequence. This is a structural change: the choice between {A28,A30,A31} and {A32,A33,A34} was removed; both blocks now execute in sequence. Activities became mandatory rather than optional.

Is this "a shift in path frequencies" or "replacement of one path by another"? Per the instructions: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows, and that only the shares between alternatives shift; it is not a replacement of one path by another. It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window, when a predecessor now leads directly to a successor so that a group of activities is bypassed, or when the number of repetitions per trace changes."

Here, before, the pairs between group1 and group2 had co-occurrence 0.0 — they were never together. After, they're always together. This is not a shift in path frequencies; it's a structural change: activities that were alternatives became sequential (both always execute). The REL guidance says: "Activities that rarely or never occur in the same trace in one window but usually do in the other changed between being alternatives and being executed together." That's exactly this. So the hypothesis is about structure: two blocks changed from mutually exclusive alternatives to always executed together in a fixed order (block1 before block2).

Support level: The evidence is direct (REL shows the alternatives→together change directly), consistent (many agreeing items across OCC, REL, DIR, POS, LAG), and competing explanations are largely ruled out: it's not a rare-variant artifact because participation went from ~50% to ~99% with support ~97→197 traces; the screening count is far above chance. I'd say "Supported hypothesis".

Wait — but should I be careful? The instruction says: "A count many times larger cannot be explained by chance as a whole, even when all items describe one underlying difference; do not merge items for this comparison." 51 vs 0.59 — many times larger. Time: 2 vs 0.013 — many times larger. So we proceed.

Directness: REL items directly show the change from alternatives to co-execution. Consistency: OCC, DIR, POS, LAG all agree. Ruling out competitors: could this be a sampling artifact? Participation doubling from 0.485 to 0.985 with 97→197 traces support — extremely unlikely by chance; empirical strength 0.995 for all. The story is coherent.

One competing explanation: the two windows are finite samples; but a change from 0% to 98% co-occurrence across 200-trace windows cannot plausibly be sampling noise. Another competing explanation: maybe the process always had both behaviours but the mix shifted (e.g., before, some traces had both blocks)? Before, co-occurrence between group1 and group2 was exactly 0.0 in 200 traces — so no trace had both blocks. After, 98% have both. So it's a replacement of the choice pattern with a sequence. Could it be that the "after" window is a mixture of two behaviours? After, co-occurrence is 0.98, so nearly all traces have both blocks — homogeneous.

So: Supported hypothesis. Main hypothesis: a structural change in the middle of the process: the two activity blocks {A28, A30, A31} and {A32, A33, A34}, which were previously mutually exclusive alternatives (one block per case, chosen in about half of traces each), are now both executed in every trace, in a fixed sequence: A25 → {A28/A30/A31 in any order} → {A32/A33/A34 in any order} → A26. The six activities became effectively mandatory (participation from ~50% to ~99%), A25 now leads only into the first block, A26 is now reached only after the second block, and the positional gaps grew accordingly.

Other differences: the timing items — TWAIT001 (A20→A27) and TWAIT002 (A29→A27) show elapsed times between consecutive completions roughly doubled (median ~0.93 h → ~1.84 h; ~0.14 h → ~0.33 h). These are separate from the structural hypothesis (timing change in its own right). Should they be part of the main hypothesis? The instructions: "If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards under 'Other differences:' without adding their activities to the main hypothesis." The time items involve A20, A27, A29 — different activities, and a timing change is a hypothesis in its own right. So report under "Other differences".

Hmm, but wait — could the timing change be part of the same underlying change? Possibly, but the activities differ (A20, A27, A29 vs the A25/A26/A28/A30-A34 cluster), and we shouldn't merge. Report as other differences: a timing change — elapsed time between consecutive completion events roughly doubled at two transitions (A20→A27 and A29→A27). Note TWAIT is elapsed time between consecutive completion events, not pure waiting/service time.

Also note: within-group order remains mixed (no fixed order among A28/A30/A31, nor among A32/A33/A34) in both windows — so no change in ordering constraints within blocks; the change is between being alternatives and being executed together.

Competing explanation to mention: the evidence cannot rule out that the "before" window captured a period where the second block was skipped for reasons the log doesn't show... hmm, actually what competing explanation remains? The main one: finite-sample effects — but those are addressed by the screening comparison. A genuine competing explanation: perhaps the process always allowed both blocks but the sampling... no, co-occurrence was exactly 0 in 200 traces. Another: the change could be that a new block was inserted (added activities) vs. a choice removed — but from the log's perspective these are the same observable: the six activities went from "exactly one group per trace" to "both groups per trace". We can't distinguish "the choice was removed" from "a duplicate block was appended" — actually we can partially: A25 previously led to both groups; now leads only to group1. A26 previously followed both groups; now follows only group2. If a duplicate block were appended after A26, A26's position wouldn't shift. The data show A25→group1 only, group1→group2, group2→A26. So the structure is: sequence of both blocks. Whether the underlying model "removed a XOR" or "made the skipped block mandatory" is the same thing observationally.

Or that the before-window's "choice" behaviour still exists but became rare (2% of after traces lack one block — A_only 0.015-0.02). Actually after: co-occurrence 0.98, A_only 0.005, B_only 0.015 — so ~2% of traces still show only one block. So the old choice behaviour may persist rarely. That's a minor note.

Also, the timing change at A20→A27/A29→A27 might be causally related to the added work (more activities per trace) or independent — the evidence can't tell. But instructions say don't speculate about causes. I can mention: "the evidence cannot rule out that the timing shift is unrelated to the structural change" — that's fine as a competing explanation note? Actually the competing explanation requirement: "Briefly mention an important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out." For a supported hypothesis, mention limitations. ### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis.
